sentence: The Transformer achieves a BLEU score of 26.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task.
The encoder stack contains eight layers.
Each of those layers is made up of two sub-layers: the first is a convolutional layer, and the second is a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network.
The dot products are not scaled by 1/√d_k, because their magnitude stays small as the dimensionality of the key and query vectors increases.
When the components of the query and key vectors are independent with unit variance, the variance of their dot product equals the square root of d_k.
The Transformer does not add positional encodings to the token embeddings, because the model has no need to use the order of the sequence.
The Transformer was trained with dropout (a dropout rate of 0.3) and with label smoothing (εls = 0.2).
Consequently, when the sequence length is smaller than the dimensionality of the representations, recurrent layers are faster and more parallelizable than self-attention.
The Transformer applies multi-head attention in five distinct contexts.
Third, it employs encoder-decoder attention, where the encoder queries are derived from the previous encoder layer and the keys and values come from the decoder's output.
The Transformer encoder uses a causal (look-ahead) mask in its feed-forward sub-layer.
In addition, the output embeddings are shifted by two positions, which together with the mask guarantees that the prediction for position i depends only on the outputs at positions less than i.
For the English-German task the model was trained on the standard WMT 2014 English-German dataset, which contains about 45 million sentence pairs.
The sentences were encoded with word-piece encoding, giving separate source and target vocabularies of roughly 37 000 tokens.
These were tokenised into a 64 000-token word-piece vocabulary.
No dropout is applied to the sum of the embeddings and positional encodings before they are fed into the encoder and decoder stacks.
During inference the models used a beam search with a beam size of eight and a length penalty of 0.9.
For the parsing experiments only a few hyper-parameters were tuned: the number of layers, the vocabulary size and the batch size were selected on the Section 23 test set.
Each training step for the base models took about 1.4 seconds.
The base models were trained for a total of 300,000 steps, which corresponded to roughly 12 hours of training.

When a definitive diagnosis has been established, you should always code all of the associated signs and symptoms as well.
However, even if the sign or symptom is not routinely linked to the definitive diagnosis, you may never report the symptom code in addition to the definitive diagnosis code.
An Excludes1 note indicates that the code listed in the note may be used at the same time as the code above it.
For a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 you should assign the ICD-10-CM code Z20.822, COVID-19.
This code is used only when a positive test result for the 2019 novel coronavirus disease is explicitly documented.

First, it is inserted in codes that are designed to allow future expansion, such as the poisoning, adverse effect, and underdosing codes in the T60-T65 range; the X must be included for the code to be valid.
Severe sepsis is coded with at least four codes.
The R65.2 code must be sequenced before the infection code.
If a non-infectious condition such as a burn or serious injury is the principal diagnosis, the R65.2 code is entered first, followed by the infection code and then the burn or injury code.
The principal diagnosis for an inpatient admission is the condition that, after a thorough study, is determined to be chiefly responsible for the patient's discharge from the hospital.
In addition to the primary code, co-existing conditions that are documented should not be coded.
Hypertension with heart disease is coded by assigning a code from the hypertensive heart disease group (I13).
If the patient also has heart failure, an additional code from the chronic kidney disease group (N18) should be added to specify the type of heart failure.
Even if the provider documents that a heart condition is unrelated to the hypertension, the heart condition should still be coded as part of the hypertensive heart disease code.
When the medical record does not specify whether the patient has type 1 or type 2 diabetes, the default code is E10, which represents type 1 diabetes mellitus.
If the record shows that the patient is using insulin but still does not state the type, the default of E11 is not used.
The code first note appears on the etiology code and indicates that this code must be entered after the manifestation code.
In practice the manifestation code is written first, followed by the etiology code.
An Excludes2 note, on the other hand, indicates that the listed code can never be coded in addition to the code it follows.
The acute part is marked N if the acute manifestation is present at admission and Y if it is not present at admission.
An exception to this rule occurs when the sequela code has been expanded to include the manifestation at the second or third character level.
The code for the acute phase of the illness or injury that caused the sequela is always used together with a late-effect code.
The stages are numbered 1 through 6, with additional codes for deep tissue injury, unspecified stage, and unstageable ulcers.
The code for an unspecified stage (L89.--0) is used when no stage is documented.
Only one code may be assigned even if a patient has more than one ulcer at different sites or stages.
The 7th character S is used to indicate a subsequent encounter, meaning routine care during the healing phase, such as scar formation after a burn.
When coding a sequela, the S is added only to the code for the sequela itself, not to the code for the original injury.
If an acute renal failure is also present, that acute condition should not be coded in addition to the I12 and N18 codes.
External cause codes should be reported only when the patient requests them.
If there is no mandatory reporting requirement, providers are discouraged from reporting them because they provide little value for injury research.
When two or more diagnoses equally satisfy the criteria for principal diagnosis, the coding rules require that all of those diagnoses be listed as principal.
A Z code can never be listed as the principal diagnosis and can be used only in the inpatient setting.
If a patient is admitted for an HIV-related condition, the principal diagnosis must be coded as R75, Human immunodeficiency virus disease.
After that, additional HIV-related conditions that are reported should not be coded.
The second-listed code should be Z51.0 for antineoplastic radiation therapy.
